subject: general
question: Raga Deepak has been associated with which famous musician?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tansen** is one of the most famous musicians in Indian history, known for his exceptional contribution to Hindustani classical music.
 
• He was one of the **Navratnas (Nine Jewels)** in the court of Emperor Akbar during the Mughal era.
 
• Tansen is associated with the **Raga Deepak**, which is known for its legend of creating fire through its rendition.
 
• According to folklore, Tansen's mastery over Raga Deepak was so profound that it could light oil lamps.
 
• He is also credited with creating several new ragas such as **Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Sarang, and Darbari Kanada.**
 
• Tansen was born in **Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh**, and initially trained under Swami Haridas, a renowned musician and saint.
 
• His contributions to Indian music are so significant that an annual **Tansen Music Festival** is held in Gwalior to honor his legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ali Khan Karori**__

 __
 
• **Naubat Khan** (also known as **Ali Khan Karori**) was an Indian classical music composer, musician and instrumentalist who was made a Mansabdar by Mughal Emperor Akbar. He is known today for his skills with the rudra veena or bīn, which he is shown playing in paintings by Mughal court artists.
 
 
 
• **Lal Kalawant**__
 __
 
• **Lal Kalawant** was a musician in the Mughal court, known for teaching Mughal Emperor Akbar the nuances of Hindu vocalization, specifically "every breathing and sound that appertains to the Hindi language". He was a musician of the Dhrupad school and was conferred the title of Gunsamundra by Shah Jahan.
 
 
 
• **Khusrau**__
 
 
• **Amir Khusrau**, a prominent Sufi poet and musician, is regarded as the father of Qawwali and credited with introducing many ragas.
 
• He lived during the Delhi Sultanate era and is also credited with the invention of instruments like the **sitar** and **tabla**.
 
• However, Khusrau is not associated with Raga Deepak, making this option incorrect.
